sections.headline: Complex products, interfaces people can operate.
sections.lead: You have been looking at a design tool and a chartering app. Both are interfaces where many dependent options have to become one clear decision. I design and build that kind of interface, from the first interaction to the details that make it work.

sections.heading: A decal editor and a chartering app share one problem
sections.text: Konfig lets riders create decals from scratch or adapt kits through colour variables, and turns the result into a print-ready PDF. Seabo turns brokers’ offer emails into data for voyage calculation, route monitoring and negotiation. Both take a specialist task with many inputs and give it a workflow people can follow.

sections.heading: The same challenge in other products

items.fit: The first Vue.js frontend for a car-offer search, built with design and UX in a young startup team.
An e-food shopping concept explored with Axure prototypes, eye tracking and other usability tests.
Comparison pages that help people make sense of the growing range of electric cars, fed by vehicle data from several sources.

sections.problem: Packaging can be complicated to configure, and the shop’s product configuration flow had to become simpler.
sections.built: As the team’s frontend and e-commerce specialist, I turned interface designs into working features on an existing Shopware theme, together with CRM API integration and delivery pipelines.
sections.result: A reported +35% conversion rate in the packaging configurator.

sections.heading: When the hard part is the data
sections.text: Public Searoutes makes sea-route calculations available without a paid service, with more than 1,000 free route calculations per month reported. It is the same kind of work as Seabo: dense professional information brought into an interface that supports a decision.
If you already have a working interface and one task users keep struggling with, a review of that single flow is the smallest useful start.

sections.heading: Which screen does everyone explain twice?
sections.text: Send a link or a screenshot of the flow that feels harder than it should. A few lines about your product are enough to start.
